Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. If contacted in relation to a job opportunity or testing, you should advise the member of the Talent Acquisition team in a timely fashion of any disabilities that requires accommodation measures in order to enable you to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner.

Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

jobs.description:
About Axya

Axya is a technology company modernizing the source-to-pay process for the manufacturing industry. Our SaaS platform streamlines and automates procurement, making it faster, simpler and more cost-effective for companies sourcing custom parts. By digitizing traditionally manual processes, Axya helps manufacturers operate with greater efficiency and competitiveness. Axya recently closed a $17 million CAD Series A funding round, a milestone that fuels our next stage of growth as we expand our team, accelerate product development and bring our platform to more manufacturers.

We are proud to cultivate an inclusive and collaborative work environment that supports innovation, growth and professional development. As a member of our team, you will work alongside passionate, forward-thinking professionals and contribute directly to transforming procurement in the manufacturing sector.

Role Overview

Axya is seeking a VP Finance to lead finance operations and guide the company through its Series B. This is a senior, hands-on role reporting directly to the CEO. You will oversee finance across Axya's two entities, secure non-dilutive funding, and prepare the company and its investors for the Series B.

Mandate And Key Responsibilities

The mandate has three components: finance operations and reporting across two entities, grants and non-dilutive financing, and pre-Series B and Series B fundraising.

Finance Operations And Reporting

Lead finance operations, month-end close, audit readiness and internal controls for both entities
Own budgeting, forecasting and runway management
Define and report key SaaS metrics, including ARR, net revenue retention, CAC payback, burn multiple and gross margin
Prepare the financial content for the board KPI pack and investor reporting
Own the finance systems
Ensure G&A and back-office costs remain in line with benchmarks for a company of Axya's revenue

Non-Dilutive Financing

Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders to secure and claim grants, R&D tax credits and government programs

Pre-Series B And Series B Fundraising

Build and maintain the financial model
Prepare the financial materials for the data room and the fundraising process
Maintain an up-to-date pipeline of prospective investors
Support day-to-day operations throughout the fundraising process
Participate in strategic meetings with investors, including travel as required
Support the CEO in term sheet negotiations

What We’re Looking For

Has led a company through a Series B financing, or has been closely involved in one
Background in supply chain, procurement or manufacturing technology, or has raised capital from investors in that space
Maintains a network of US-based investors relevant to Axya's Series B
Proven experience in finance operations and in investor and board reporting
Has negotiated debt and equity financing terms and can support the CEO throughout a Series B process
Willing to travel to meet investors

Being based in the US is not a requirement. Access to US investors and a willingness to travel are.

Why Join Axya

🏖 Unlimited vacation policy: because we believe in balance.
🏥 Comprehensive health insurance: your well-being matters.
🕒 Flexible work schedule: results matter more than hours
🏡 100% remote: get the job done wherever you prefer.
🚀 Be part of a high-impact, collaborative team making real change in a traditional industry.

Company Description
Slemon Park Corporation owns and manages a vibrant business and residential community in Prince Edward Island, Canada, offering integrated spaces to work, live, and learn. Established in 1992 following the transfer and redevelopment of the former CFB Summerside, the corporation has transformed the military base into a globally competitive business park focused on aerospace, manufacturing, and public safety training. The community spans 1,400 acres and includes more than 830,000 square feet of commercial and training facilities, featuring six aircraft hangars. Slemon Park hosts over 20 commercial tenants employing approximately 1,100 people, alongside a residential community of more than 230 families. Amenities such as the Summerside Airport, hotel and conference centre, restaurant and pub, health centre, and convenience store create a complete, self-contained environment for businesses and residents.
Role Description
The Vice President Finance Administration is a full-time, on-site position based in Slemon Park, PE, responsible for overseeing the corporation’s financial strategy, administrative operations, and long-term sustainability. This role manages financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting, ensuring accurate preparation and analysis of financial statements and compliance with applicable regulations and policies. The Vice President provides leadership to finance and administrative teams, establishes controls and procedures, and supports audit, risk management, and governance activities. Day-to-day responsibilities include monitoring cash flow, capital expenditures, and operational costs; preparing reports and presentations for senior leadership and the Board; and contributing to strategic initiatives, investment decisions, and business partnerships. The role also collaborates closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to support the growth and effective management of Slemon Park’s business and residential community.
Qualifications

Strong finance and budgeting skills, including experience in Finance, Budgeting, and Financial Planning.
Proficiency in preparing, analyzing, and interpreting Financial Statements, with solid Analytical Skills.
Demonstrated leadership experience in senior finance or administration roles, preferably in real estate, infrastructure, or community-based organizations.
Knowledge of Canadian accounting standards, financial controls, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to non-financial audiences.
Proven ability to manage teams, develop processes, and drive operational efficiency in finance and administrative functions.
Relevant post-secondary education in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field; professional designation (e.g., CPA, CMA) is considered an asset.
Comfort working on-site within a multi-faceted business and residential community and collaborating with government, business, and community partners.

jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
jobs.description:
Supplier.io is the data foundation that enterprises build their supplier decisions on. Fragmented, duplicated, and unreliable supplier data quietly limits the ROI of source-to-pay platforms, analytics, risk, and AI initiatives, so we resolve, enrich, and continuously maintain the industry's most complete supplier identity, then put it to work for the teams that buy and the suppliers themselves. Relied on by companies across the Fortune 2000 for accurate data, our platform helps corporate procurement, finance, and compliance teams manage their vendor master, source diverse and sustainable suppliers, and mitigate risk, all from one verified identity instead of a dozen disconnected systems.

Our solutions turn that foundation into action: accurate data and continuous maintenance for teams managing a fragmented vendor master, sourcing intelligence built resolving even the hardest-to-identify suppliers, small, local, and diverse businesses, for teams tracking sustainability and compliance, and direct visibility for the suppliers themselves into where they stand with the enterprises that buy from them. Whether you're resolving vendor records, sourcing alternatives, or measuring program results, Supplier.io transforms complexity into clarity, so teams can lead with confidence and build supply chains that deliver for both business and community.

For more information, visit www.supplier.io.

The Opportunity

The Director, Data Architecture owns the strategy, standards, and team behind how data moves through Supplier.io, from source systems and web-scraping pipelines through ingestion, transformation, and governed delivery into the warehouses and marts the rest of the business relies on. You'll operate as a peer to our other engineering leaders, setting data architecture direction jointly with the CTO, while staying accountable for the reliability, quality, and governance of every data workflow we run.

You'll lead two distinct groups: a Data Engineering team building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and a Data Operations Engineering team running and maintaining the processes already in production. In the near term, before the team and its processes are fully built out, this role is hands-on: you'll be designing pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly, not just directing from a distance.

What You Will Do

Data Architecture & Platform Strategy

Own the multi-year data architecture strategy across our data warehouses and operational data stores, including evolving toward a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) lakehouse model.
Design and own our data lake and warehouse architecture, including the formation and population of data marts that serve analytics, product, and stakeholder reporting needs.
Set the orchestration strategy and standards for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT, and automated workflow management, and standardize the tooling used across the function.
Own the infrastructure and administration behind our data warehouses and pipelines, including capacity, reliability, and cost.
Own data governance end to end: the policies, standards, and practices for data quality, lineage, access, retention, and classification across every system of record.

Team & Execution Leadership

Build, lead, and grow two functions: Data Engineering, building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, running and maintaining existing production data processes.
Decide how the function is organized as it scales, including when and whether to add management layers beneath you to run day-to-day execution.
Stay hands-on early: design and review pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly until the team is built out to carry that execution independently, and stay close enough to the technology afterward to make credible architecture calls.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with engineering leadership to keep data architecture decisions aligned with company-wide standards.
Work closely with data engineering teams on technical planning and delivery for our core data products.
Partner with product, analytics, and other business stakeholders across the company to understand data needs and translate them into warehouse and data mart designs.

Data Quality & Compliance

Define and enforce data quality gates, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Own data access controls, classification, and retention policy across the data estate.
Ensure compliance-relevant and audit-sensitive data is handled according to governance standards as our data sources and customer base grow.

What You Will Need To Succeed

10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, including 5+ years in a Director or Manager-level leadership role owning architecture strategy and a team, not just individual delivery.
Deep, hands-on experience designing and operating cloud data warehouse or lakehouse architectures (Snowflake and/or BigQuery), including medallion (bronze, silver, gold) patterns.
Experience integrating a range of source systems (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and building ingestion and ETL pipelines from varied and unstructured sources, including web-scraping pipelines and background job orchestration.
A track record of building and scaling a data engineering or data platform organization, including deciding when and how to split engineering and operations functions.
Strong data governance background: establishing policies and standards for data quality, lineage, access, and retention in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment.
Experience setting technical direction jointly with peer engineering leaders and influencing architecture decisions across teams.
Excellent communication skills, comfortable setting strategy with peer leaders and reporting data platform health, cost, and risk directly to the CTO.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating or re-architecting data platforms following an acquisition or significant data source expansion.
Experience with orchestration tooling such as Airflow or dbt, and with scraping or crawling infrastructure at scale.
Background establishing data marts and self-service analytics layers for non-engineering stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability tooling (Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar).

jobs.title: Vice President of Programs
jobs.description:
We’re Recruiting For…

Vice President of Programs

About the Centre 

The Confederation Centre is Canada’s National Memorial to the founders of the country. It is the result of a dream shared by all Canadians - a place where Canada’s evolution and multicultural character is celebrated and explored right where Canadian confederation began; where the talents of Canadian people are nurtured and showcased through arts, learning, and conversation. Taking up a full city block in downtown Charlottetown, the Centre includes performance venues, art gallery spaces, arts education and learning studios, and spaces for convening and conversation. 

Opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1964 to commemorate the centennial of the 1864 Charlottetown Conference, the Confederation Centre has welcomed millions of visitors from Canada and the world to experience Canada through many lenses. Producing world-class theatre performances, gallery exhibitions, arts education, community programs, and convening opportunities for discussion on Canadian confederation, the Centre is the largest national multidisciplinary cultural institution in Atlantic Canada. 

Home to the Charlottetown Festival, which sells close to 100,000 tickets over 14 weeks each summer, the Centre employs more than 200 people and drives more than $30 million in economic activity for Prince Edward Island. The Centre is now completing the most signiﬁcant transformation in its history: a $65 million rejuvenation of the former library and archives complex, creating new facilities for the Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, the Arts Academy, and the Arts Innovation Hub. The Centre is governed by a national board of directors from across Canada. It is where people learn about Canada and explore the issues most important to us; it is Where Canada Connects. 

Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island 

The capital city of PEI is the birthplace of Canadian confederation, and the Confederation Centre of the Arts is Canada’s national memorial to those who met here in 1864 and proposed a union that would result in a new country three years later. Charlottetown is a beautiful place to live and work. It has a thriving cultural community with numerous attractions including arts, recreation, restaurants, parks, and the harbour. Charlottetown is home to the University of Prince Edward Island and Holland College, and welcomes roughly 1.5 million tourists every summer. Minutes away are some of the best beaches, golf courses, and natural attractions that Canada has to oﬀer. 

The Opportunity

The Confederation Centre is seeking a Vice President of Programs, to lead and support all of the Centre’s public programming. Reporting to the Chief Executive Oﬃcer, the Vice President of Programs provides leadership to the program directors and staﬀ in Theatre, Art Gallery, Arts Academy, Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, Archives, and the Arts Innovation Hub, to ensure sustainable operations and positive impact locally, regionally, and nationally.  

As the Centre completes the most signiﬁcant expansion in its history, its programming is growing in scale and in range. The Vice President will ensure this growth is coordinated, ﬁnancially sustainable, and aligned with the Centre’s Strategic Plan, so that every program contributes to the Centre’s national mandate and mission.

new_jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
new_jobs.description:
Supplier.io is the data foundation that enterprises build their supplier decisions on. Fragmented, duplicated, and unreliable supplier data quietly limits the ROI of source-to-pay platforms, analytics, risk, and AI initiatives, so we resolve, enrich, and continuously maintain the industry's most complete supplier identity, then put it to work for the teams that buy and the suppliers themselves. Relied on by companies across the Fortune 2000 for accurate data, our platform helps corporate procurement, finance, and compliance teams manage their vendor master, source diverse and sustainable suppliers, and mitigate risk, all from one verified identity instead of a dozen disconnected systems.

Our solutions turn that foundation into action: accurate data and continuous maintenance for teams managing a fragmented vendor master, sourcing intelligence built resolving even the hardest-to-identify suppliers, small, local, and diverse businesses, for teams tracking sustainability and compliance, and direct visibility for the suppliers themselves into where they stand with the enterprises that buy from them. Whether you're resolving vendor records, sourcing alternatives, or measuring program results, Supplier.io transforms complexity into clarity, so teams can lead with confidence and build supply chains that deliver for both business and community.

For more information, visit www.supplier.io.

The Opportunity

The Director, Data Architecture owns the strategy, standards, and team behind how data moves through Supplier.io, from source systems and web-scraping pipelines through ingestion, transformation, and governed delivery into the warehouses and marts the rest of the business relies on. You'll operate as a peer to our other engineering leaders, setting data architecture direction jointly with the CTO, while staying accountable for the reliability, quality, and governance of every data workflow we run.

You'll lead two distinct groups: a Data Engineering team building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and a Data Operations Engineering team running and maintaining the processes already in production. In the near term, before the team and its processes are fully built out, this role is hands-on: you'll be designing pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly, not just directing from a distance.

What You Will Do

Data Architecture & Platform Strategy

Own the multi-year data architecture strategy across our data warehouses and operational data stores, including evolving toward a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) lakehouse model.
Design and own our data lake and warehouse architecture, including the formation and population of data marts that serve analytics, product, and stakeholder reporting needs.
Set the orchestration strategy and standards for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT, and automated workflow management, and standardize the tooling used across the function.
Own the infrastructure and administration behind our data warehouses and pipelines, including capacity, reliability, and cost.
Own data governance end to end: the policies, standards, and practices for data quality, lineage, access, retention, and classification across every system of record.

Team & Execution Leadership

Build, lead, and grow two functions: Data Engineering, building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, running and maintaining existing production data processes.
Decide how the function is organized as it scales, including when and whether to add management layers beneath you to run day-to-day execution.
Stay hands-on early: design and review pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly until the team is built out to carry that execution independently, and stay close enough to the technology afterward to make credible architecture calls.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with engineering leadership to keep data architecture decisions aligned with company-wide standards.
Work closely with data engineering teams on technical planning and delivery for our core data products.
Partner with product, analytics, and other business stakeholders across the company to understand data needs and translate them into warehouse and data mart designs.

Data Quality & Compliance

Define and enforce data quality gates, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Own data access controls, classification, and retention policy across the data estate.
Ensure compliance-relevant and audit-sensitive data is handled according to governance standards as our data sources and customer base grow.

What You Will Need To Succeed

10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, including 5+ years in a Director or Manager-level leadership role owning architecture strategy and a team, not just individual delivery.
Deep, hands-on experience designing and operating cloud data warehouse or lakehouse architectures (Snowflake and/or BigQuery), including medallion (bronze, silver, gold) patterns.
Experience integrating a range of source systems (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and building ingestion and ETL pipelines from varied and unstructured sources, including web-scraping pipelines and background job orchestration.
A track record of building and scaling a data engineering or data platform organization, including deciding when and how to split engineering and operations functions.
Strong data governance background: establishing policies and standards for data quality, lineage, access, and retention in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment.
Experience setting technical direction jointly with peer engineering leaders and influencing architecture decisions across teams.
Excellent communication skills, comfortable setting strategy with peer leaders and reporting data platform health, cost, and risk directly to the CTO.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating or re-architecting data platforms following an acquisition or significant data source expansion.
Experience with orchestration tooling such as Airflow or dbt, and with scraping or crawling infrastructure at scale.
Background establishing data marts and self-service analytics layers for non-engineering stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability tooling (Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar).

About the Centre 

The Confederation Centre is Canada’s National Memorial to the founders of the country. Taking up a full city block in downtown Charlottetown, the Centre includes performance venues, art gallery spaces, arts education and learning studios, and spaces for convening and conversation. 

Opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1964 to commemorate the centennial of the 1864 Charlottetown Conference, the Confederation Centre has welcomed millions of visitors from Canada and the world to experience Canada through many lenses. Producing world-class theatre performances, gallery exhibitions, arts education, community programs, and convening opportunities for discussion on Canadian confederation, the Centre is the largest national multidisciplinary cultural institution in Atlantic Canada. 

Home to the Charlottetown Festival, which sells close to 100,000 tickets over 14 weeks each summer, the Centre employs more than 200 people and drives more than $30 million in economic activity for Prince Edward Island. The Centre is now completing the most signiﬁcant transformation in its history: a $65 million rejuvenation of the former library and archives complex, creating new facilities for the Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, the Arts Academy, and the Arts Innovation Hub. The Centre is governed by a national board of directors from across Canada. It is where people learn about Canada and explore the issues most important to us; it is Where Canada Connects.
